title: The open-complement condition from the direct-image input
statement:
Let $k$ be the algebraic closure of a finite field, let $d\in\mathbf Z_{\geq0}$, let $T$ be a finite-type $k$-scheme of Krull dimension at most $d$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism; def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], and let $j:V\hookrightarrow T$ be a quasi-compact open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion]. Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring annihilated by a power of a prime $\ell\neq\operatorname{char}(k)$. Then the pair $(V,T)$ satisfies the open-complement condition at $A$ of [def-exc-open-complement-bound] with $c=2d$.
Independently of the general argument, the condition holds in dimension zero because an open immersion into a zero-dimensional Noetherian scheme (locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth] and quasi-compact) is also a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] and its direct image is exact extension by zero, preserving constructibility. In dimension at most one, [thm-exc-curve-open-dimension-general] and [thm-exc-curve-open-constructible-general] give the independent vanishing and constructibility assertions (with vanishing already for $q>1$).

proof.text: The algebraic closure k is algebraically closed and hence separably closed. The prime ell is nonzero in k and therefore a unit; map this unit through the global sections map to T. If ell^n kills 1_A, it kills every a in A by multiplication, including the zero ring. Replace n by n+1 for a positive exponent when needed.

The quasi-compact open immersion j is finite type; compositions of finite-type morphisms make V finite type over k. Its inducing map gives dim V <= dim T <= d directly, without constructing affine covers.

Apply clause (1) of the direct-image finiteness input to j and the signed annihilator ell^n. For a nonnegative integer degree write q=m with m natural and compare the unbounded and bounded-below right-derived functors using rightDerivedFunctorPlusCompatibility. Transfer constructibility along the homology isomorphism using the equivalence of constructible module sheaf predicates. In negative degrees use right-derived negative vanishing and constructibility of a zero sheaf.

The finite additive group of A is torsion. Apply isZero_higherDirectImage_of_two_mul_lt to j, the structure maps of V and T and the bound on dim V, obtaining zero in all integer degrees q>2d. Together with constructibility this is exactly HasOpenComplementCondition A j (2*d). This reuses the existing module-level torsion vanishing theorem instead of repeating its affine-etale and sheafification proof.

Independently in dimension zero, finite type over the Noetherian Spec k makes T locally Noetherian and compact. The finite-discrete theorem makes its topology discrete. Hence the image of j is closed, and the open immersion is a closed immersion by IsClosedImmersion.of_isPreimmersion. The canonical extension-by-zero to direct-image comparison is an isomorphism for this closed image. Transport finite-colimit preservation from extension by zero. Extension by zero preserves constructibility; transport this along the comparison and the equivalence of constructible module sheaf predicates.

For the now exact direct image functor, use its existing singleFunctorCompRightDerivedFunctorIso API to identify the total derived image of M[0] with (j_* M)[0]; first compare bounded-below and unbounded right-derived functors. A single-degree object has zero homology in every degree q different from zero by its IsGE 0 and IsLE 0 instances. At degree zero its homology is j_* M by singleFunctorCompHomologyFunctorIso. Transport constructibility from the previous step in degree zero and from the zero sheaf in the remaining degrees. This proves the bound zero independently of the general direct-image input.

Independently in dimension at most one, use the two stated curve theorems with the mapped unit ell and the positive annihilator exponent. Their conclusions are respectively the vanishing and constructibility conjuncts of the bound one. The arguments apply also to empty schemes.

blueprint_update.statement:
Let $k$ be the algebraic closure of a finite field, let $T$ be a
finite-type $k$-scheme of dimension at most $d$, let
$j:V\hookrightarrow T$ be a
quasi-compact open immersion,
and let $A$ be a finite ring annihilated by a power of a prime
$\ell\neq\operatorname{char}(k)$. Then the pair $(V,T)$ satisfies the
open-complement condition of [def-exc-open-complement-bound] with
$c=2d$.
Independently of the general argument, the condition is immediate in
dimension zero, where an open immersion of a zero-dimensional Noetherian
scheme is also closed, and it holds in dimension at most one by
[thm-exc-curve-open-dimension-general], [thm-exc-curve-open-constructible-general].

proof.text:
The field $k$ is separably closed, so both clauses of the direct-image
finiteness input hold over $k$ by
[thm-exc-direct-image-input-holds]. The constructibility clause is
its clause (1) applied to the open immersion $j$,
which is of finite type because it is quasi-compact and $T$ is of finite
type over $k$.
For the vanishing clause, fix a geometric point $\bar t$ of $T$. The
strict-henselization stalk formula
[prop-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-stalk-formula] identifies the
stalk of the higher direct image with the cohomology of the open
complement over the strict henselization at $\bar t$,

$$
\bigl(R^qj_*M\bigr)_{\bar t}
\;\cong\;H^q\bigl(V\times_TT_{(\bar t)},M\bigr),
$$

a filtered colimit of the groups $H^q(V\times_TU,M)$ over the pointed
etale neighbourhoods $U\to T$ of $\bar t$; each $V\times_TU$ is an
open subscheme of the etale $T$-scheme $U$, hence a finite-type
$k$-scheme of dimension at most $d$. As $k$ is separably closed,
clause (2) of that input gives
$H^q(V\times_TU,M)=0$ for $q>2d$ and every torsion sheaf $M$, and
vanishing is preserved by the filtered colimit. Hence every geometric
stalk of $R^qj_*M$ vanishes for $q>2d$, and conservativity of
geometric stalks ([lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative]) makes
the sheaf itself zero, which is the vanishing clause with $c=2d$.
